To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(I) the strength of intermediate beams in SPSW systems should be increased to resist forces imposed by fully yielding plates; (II) the strength of foundation beams in SPSWs should be increased to prevent in-span plastic hinges; and (III), the strength of roof beams in SPSWS should be increased to avoid in-span plastic hinges when a collapse mechanism is developing.

(I) the design of intermediate beams in SPSWs should be based on forces determined by the fully yielded plates, and (II) the design of the roof and foundation beam should be based on the design of the SPSWs as a whole.

(a) in-span plastic hinges can develop in intermediate beams of SPSW models when these beams are designed according to criteria (I) and (II); (b) in-span plastic hinge formation can be avoided by increasing the design strength of the intermediate beams; (c) the design strength of intermediate beams should be at least equal to the strength of the plates; and (d) the design of intermediate beams should not be based on CAN/CSA-S16-01.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the design of SPSW intermediate beams needs to be carefully considered, and that the current design provisions are not sufficient to avoid the formation in-span plastic hinges.

, in order to avoid in-span plastic hinges and to minimize the development of collapse mechanisms, the design of SPSW intermediate beams should be based on criteria that take into consideration the forces that the plates can reach in a severe seismic event.
, for the design of intermediate beams in SPSWs, the design forces should be determined based on the assumption that the plates at the beam level are fully yielded.
